value: more detections of individuals during daylight hours
method: passive acoustic telemetry (Vemco VR2W receiver array); detections compared among dawn, day, dusk and night
conditions: Wild adult trumpet emperor line-caught, tagged and released at the northern reef slope of Heron Island Reef, southern Great Barrier Reef; eleven fish tagged, seven detected over 93 days (22 March to 22 June 2014), five detected consistently and analysed for space use; the paper does not state which individuals entered the time-of-day detection comparison. The measure is acoustic detection counts, not tracked activity, and the paper's sentinel-tag standardisation indicated absence during crepuscular and night periods was not an artefact of transmitter detectability. Contrary space-use result from the same fish: horizontal core areas and vertical areas of extent were significantly larger at crepuscular and night periods than during the day (not filed as a diel value here).
